notes: Everything is in rounds/tester.py: result_records (run for GET and again under the round lock for POST) reads only the signed-in tester's result and raises Unavailable for a non-Open round, a superseded build and, on POST, a submitted result; result_page builds no form for a submitted result. There is no service layer. ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation (no database constraint) and ObservationField sets max_length=2000, so M5 raises only that and its fixed message is unchanged. M4's page shows the form with 'Status: Submitted' (Result.status). M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard). M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005 to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
